questions.question: How long does a station last on batteries when it measures every ten minutes?
questions.reference: About 14 months on two 18650 cells (accelerated simulation).
questions.answer:
The only figure in Flux is from Piotr Zieliński's battery test (May 22, 2026, in the Czujniki space's conversation with Jonas and Marta): a station measuring every 10 minutes lasted **14 months on two 18650 cells**. He labelled it an accelerated simulation, so it is not a field measurement.

Field reports since then suggest real batteries run lower than that. Stations at Zaspa, Wrzeszcz and Przymorze dropped to 5–20% charge in March to November, and firmware changes since May (2.5.x) changed the reporting interval. I found no measured field runtime at a 10-minute interval. Tell me if you want me to search the sensor sleep-current or solar-panel threads for more.

bateria stacja pomiar co 10 minut wystarczy

judge.reason: The answer states the reference's key fact, 14 months on two 18650 cells at a 10-minute interval from an accelerated simulation, and does not contradict it; the extra field-report commentary is additional detail rather than a conflicting value.

questions.question: Co się działo w tej przestrzeni w zeszłym tygodniu, od poniedziałku do niedzieli?
questions.reference: Co najmniej dwa z trzech: uszkodzone kartony w palecie obudów od Plastmetu (reklamacja); inwentaryzacja w Pruszczu przesunięta na 20-tego; umowa z Raben na transport palet do Gdańska. Inne wydarzenia z tamtego tygodnia mogą też być wymienione.
questions.answer:
W zeszłym tygodniu (pon. 2 – niedz. 8 listopada) w przestrzeni było 41 wiadomości. Najważniejsze:

- **Wysyłki i klienci:** kilka paczek do klientów wyszło (2, 3, 4 i 5 listopada), a 40 stacji zapowiedziano na wtorek 3 listopada. 25 stacji dla Gdańska odbierze InPost w czwartek 13 listopada.
- **Dostawy i reklamacje:** paleta obudów od Plastmetu dotarła 3 listopada z 3 uszkodzonymi kartonami, reklamacja poszła z dokumentacją. Reklamacja do Ecoprimy wysłana 4 listopada, a do Farnella 6 listopada; obie czekają na odpowiedź.
- **Ceny:** TME (+40%), Mouser (+15%, potem +24%), DigiKey (+10%) i Farnell (+3%) podnoszą ceny od następnego miesiąca.
- **Magazyn:** inwentaryzacja była wielokrotnie zapowiadana (czwartek, piątek, poniedziałek, środa), a w Pruszczu przesunięto ją na 20 listopada, bo wózek widłowy jest w serwisie. Zaksięgowano faktury od Ecoprimy i Plastmetu.
- **Sprawy otwarte:** problemy celne (odprawa trwała 2–3 dni, dzwoni się do agencji) i zgłoszony problem z VPN-em.

Zakres obejmuje tylko wiadomości z wątku przestrzeni do 7 listopada rano; nie sprawdzałem zadań ani dokumentów.

questions.question: What happened in this space last week, Monday to Sunday?
questions.reference: At least two of three: the fonts were self-hosted and the CDN removed; the newsletter moved from Mailchimp to Brevo; the cookie banner was removed because Plausible needs no consent. Other events of that week may be named too.
questions.answer:
Last week (Mon 2 to Sun 8 November) the space had 30 messages, and the digest covers all of them. The main threads were:

- **Performance:** Lighthouse scores were reported for about (6), careers (24) and pricing (10, later 6). Mobile load times were flagged as too slow for careers (15 s) and pricing (24 s). Jonas self-hosted the fonts and removed the CDN.
- **Content and review:** Several pages were updated and proofreading was requested for the home, product, pricing and contact pages. A new hero image for pricing was added in Figma.
- **Legal and analytics:** Jonas reported that the cookie banner was removed, since Plausible needs no consent and legal confirmed this. Cookie text still needed a lawyer's review before launch.
- **Operations:** The newsletter moved from Mailchimp to Brevo with 340 subscribers. Staging went down again and was redeployed. The contact form was catching spam again. The about page moved under /product, and so did the product page.
- **Open questions:** Who owns the blog posts on green roofs and air quality, and where the Hetzner and Google Workspace docs live.

judge.reason: The answer states all three reference facts: fonts self-hosted with the CDN removed, newsletter moved from Mailchimp to Brevo, and cookie banner removed because Plausible needs no consent, meeting the at-least-two requirement.
